doc.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Marketing, promotion and the musicians' respect for Alfred
summary: She did PR and artist promotion; Alfred's accounting background and concentration made musicians play their best on his dates.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So when the label was first launched, then the whole idea of distribution and selling it and all of that comes into play.
Did he have any experience in marketing? Did you have any experience in marketing that you later helped him with?

Well yes I did public relations and artist promotion for him. However, himself he just had a natural intellect. He had, in Germany, learned accounting and he was just, as I said before, a very careful, caring person. His concentration was so that it couldn’t be broken. I mean that was why I was saying that with Billie Holiday that, “Don’t come into my recording session,” and, “I mean we’re here for business.” And what Dexter Gordon said, “You just have to play better for Blue Note.” When the guys came on a Blue Note date, they knew, everybody was going to do their best. You know they loved him and they wanted to do their best. And they did. That’s why so many of the records are considered very, very much classic.
